Between-Sample (Beta) Diversity of microbes in dairy samples across seasons

Kailyn Hanke

2025-04-26

#Goals

The goal of this document is to run an analysis on the between-sample (beta( diversity of the samples in my project, similar to the analysis that I ran in 06_Ordination. This is the second of three new analysis documents I will make (I have previously made 08_Seasonal_Biodiversity and will subsequently make 10_Seasonality_Composition). See more info on my organizational layout under “Goals” in 08_Seasonal_Biodiversity.

Unlike in my original 06_Ordination analysis, I do not need to evaluate sequencing depth and normalize read counts, as I have previously done this in my original homework document!

In particular, I’m hoping that this seasonal/sample analysis will explain the weird grouping in my Skimmed Milk Powder samples.

  1. Calculate community dissimilarities. Numbers between 0 and 1. If 0, completely similar versus if they are 1, then they’re completely dissimilar. Here I will split up my communities by sample type AND season!!
    1. Sorensen: Shared Species as a binary value: Abundance-unweighted
    2. Bray-Curtis: Shared Abundant species: Abundance-weighted
    3. (Abundance-)Weighted UNIFRAC: Consider Abundant Species and where they fall on the tree
  2. Run statistics with functions from the vegan R package:
    1. PERMANOVA with adonis2().
    2. betadispR with betadisper() and permutest().
  3. Visualize the community data with two unconstrained Ordinations:
    1. PCoA: Linear Method. Eigenvalue = how much variation is explained by each axis. Choose to view axis 1, 2, 3, etc. and plot them together.
    2. NMDS: Non-linear. Smush multiple Dimensions into 2 or 3 axes. Need to report Stress value (ideally <0.15).

Inputs

  1. We will need the scaled_physeq.RData, that we created in analysis/06_Ordination.Rmd.

Outputs

While defining community based on sample type and season: 1. Calculated beta-diversity dissimilarity measures (e.g. Sorensen, Bray-Curtis, abundance-unweighted and -weighted UniFrac) across every sample. 2. Ordination figures (i.e., PCoA/NMDS) to include in the scientific paper that visualize the data as it relates to the scientific question. 3. Statistical tests (i.e., PERMANOVA & betadisper) conveying the measured and quantified changes and patterns in biodiversity.

Set up

Timing of this script

# What time did we start running this script? 
start_time <- Sys.time()

Set the seed

set.seed(111111)

Load Packages, colors & functions

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, devtools, phyloseq, patchwork, vegan, 
               install = FALSE)

# Load Colors 
source("code/colors.R")

# Load functions 
source("code/functions.R")

1. Load in the data

load("data/06_Ordination/scaled_physeq.RData")

read.csv("data/06_Ordination/metadata_df_cut20000.csv")

Beta Diversity: Dissimilarity Metrics in Microbial Ecology

Calculating dissimilarity

Now, let’s make distance objects of the dissimiliarity measures we used in class!

# Sorensen Dissimiliarty
scaled_sorensen_dist <- phyloseq::distance(scaled_physeq, method = "bray", binary = TRUE)

# Bray-Curtis Dissimiliarty
scaled_bray_dist <- phyloseq::distance(scaled_physeq, method = "bray", binary = FALSE)

# Abundance-Unweighted UniFrac
scaled_uUnifrac_dist <- phyloseq::distance(scaled_physeq, method = "unifrac")

# Abundance-Weighted UniFrac
scaled_wUnifrac_dist <- phyloseq::distance(scaled_physeq, method = "wunifrac")

PERMANOVA: Testing Means/Centroids

Here, we will focus on comparing the Sorensen and the Bray-Curtis.

First I will mutate my metadata to include a new column season to define mid- and late-lactation.

# Create a new column 'season' based on the Collection_Date
metadata_df_season <- metadata_df_cut20000 %>%
  mutate(season = case_when(
    month(as.Date(Collection_Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")) == 5 ~ "mid-lactation",  # May is mid-lactation
    TRUE ~ "late-lactation"  # All other months are late-lactation
  ))

# Check if the new column is created correctly
table(metadata_df_season$season)
## 
## late-lactation  mid-lactation 
##             87             98
glimpse(metadata_df_season)

Betadisper: Testing Variances/Dispersions

Sorensen

# Homogeneity of Disperson test with beta dispr

# Sorensen Betadisper - Sample Type 
dispr_sorensen_sample <- betadisper(scaled_sorensen_dist, metadata_df_season$environment_material)
# permutest() performs a non-parametric permutation test, which is robust and valid for the kind of data used in beta diversity analysis (e.g., dissimilarity matrices).

permutest(dispr_sorensen_sample)

Sorensen

# First, calculate PCoA with Soresen
scaled_soren_pcoa <- 
  ordinate(physeq = scaled_physeq,
         method = "PCoA",
         distance = "bray", binary = TRUE)

# Take a quick look
str(scaled_soren_pcoa)
## List of 5
##  $ correction: chr [1:2] "none" "1"
##  $ note      : chr "There were no negative eigenvalues. No correction was applied"
##  $ values    :'data.frame':  184 obs. of  5 variables:
##   ..$ Eigenvalues   : num [1:184] 6.54 2.5 1.74 1.29 1.02 ...
##   ..$ Relative_eig  : num [1:184] 0.0923 0.0353 0.0246 0.0183 0.0144 ...
##   ..$ Broken_stick  : num [1:184] 0.0315 0.0261 0.0233 0.0215 0.0202 ...
##   ..$ Cumul_eig     : num [1:184] 0.0923 0.1276 0.1522 0.1704 0.1848 ...
##   ..$ Cumul_br_stick: num [1:184] 0.0315 0.0576 0.0809 0.1024 0.1226 ...
##  $ vectors   : num [1:185, 1:184] -0.0906 -0.1316 0.0514 0.0626 -0.134 ...
##   ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
##   .. ..$ : chr [1:185] "ERR3141386" "ERR3141387" "ERR3141388" "ERR3141389" ...
##   .. ..$ : chr [1:184] "Axis.1" "Axis.2" "Axis.3" "Axis.4" ...
##  $ trace     : num 70.8
##  - attr(*, "class")= chr "pcoa"
# Plot it: Sorensen PCoA  
sorensen_pcoa_plot <- 
  plot_ordination(physeq = scaled_physeq,
                ordination = scaled_soren_pcoa,
                color = "environment_material",
                shape = "season",
                title = "Sorensen PCoA") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = environment_colors) + 
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(15, 16)) + 
  geom_point(size = 5, alpha = 0.5, aes(color = environment_material)) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "right")
